how_it_was_found: Running the hosted service check against the live deployment after billing was switched on. It passed 3 of 16, then 13 of 16, before passing 16 of 16.

findings.what: The diagnostic service keys had expired.
findings.detail: They are issued with a lifetime of one day on purpose, and nothing reissued them. Every authenticated hosted check failed with a refusal that looked the same as a wrong key.
findings.why_it_matters: An operator cannot tell an expired credential from a broken service without looking, and the checks that prove the deployment works stop working a day after they are set up.
findings.fix: tools/reissue_service_keys.py asks the running service for a new key using the administrator credential already held, and writes it straight back into the keyring. The value is never printed, never written to a file and never put on a command line. It requires an explicit confirmation, refuses an address that is not an exact secure origin, refuses a lifetime outside one minute to seven days, and leaves the saved value untouched when the service refuses.
findings.checks: Ten, including that a refused issue writes nothing, that storage which does not confirm is reported rather than assumed, and a known-wrong control showing that dropping the scope list would widen the key.

findings.what: The operator entitlements had expired, so no body could be read.
findings.detail: Both diagnostic accounts held a grant that ended on 20 September. Searching and listing still worked, so the service looked healthy, but every download was refused and no usage was recorded.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the shape of a silent customer outage. The account is enabled, sign-in works, search works, and only the thing the customer pays for stops. Nothing announced it.
findings.fix: Both grants were renewed for ninety days from the host configuration, which is the declared source for them. The renewal used the existing host grant path, not a new one.
findings.still_open: Nothing reports an approaching expiry. A paid account renews through its subscription, but an operator granted account does not, so an operator has no warning before access stops. This belongs with the reliability work.

a_defect_found_while_writing_the_check.what: The scope list of a reissued key was a default argument, captured when the file was imported.
a_defect_found_while_writing_the_check.why_it_matters: Narrowing the list in one place would not have narrowed the keys, and the control that was meant to prove the narrowing could not see it either.
a_defect_found_while_writing_the_check.fix: The list is read when the command runs.
